validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: confirmed independently. ETIH's own Oct 17, 2024 non-binding Open Season notice and its Nov 15, 2024 timeline-extension notice (both live on pipelines.energytransfer.com, both name 'South Mississippi Project' explicitly) are corroborated by East Daley Analytics' independent Oct 31, 2024 trade-press piece ('Midstream Projects Compete for New Demand in Southeast'), which describes the same project, same capacity (1.0 Bcf/d scalable to 2.0 Bcf/d), same 2Q28 in-service target, and same Carthage/Perryville-to-FGT-Zone-3 routing. This is not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas transmission -- it is explicitly an interstate, FERC-jurisdictional firm-transportation project ('ETIH... will require... Federal Energy Regulatory Commission authorization'), not a gathering/distribution line. DUPLICATE: checked against the roster's other Mississippi-corridor rows. P7802 (Tennessee Gas Pipeline / 'Mississippi Crossing (MSX)') and P7841 ('Mississippi Crossing Project') are a SEPARATE Kinder Morgan/TGP project (Greenville MS -> Butler AL, FERC Docket CP25-514-000, certificated 2026-07-31) with a different sponsor, route, and docket from ETIH's South Mississippi Project (Carthage TX/Haynesville/Perryville -> FGT Zone 3 near Sonat) -- similar name and overlapping Southeast-demand rationale, but not the same pipe (see cross_row_leads for what I found on the Mississippi Crossing docket, useful for whichever shard works P7802/P7841). No FERC CP docket was found for 'South Mississippi Project' itself as of a Sept 2026 search (elibrary/Federal Register/news), consistent with its EIA 'Announced'/pre-filing status -- the more advanced Kinder Morgan projects in the same corridor already have dockets, which is a useful contrast, not evidence this row is stale or non-existent.

The sheet's 1000 MMcf/d is well-sourced as the announced base case (see the Capacity fill), but EIA's more recent tracking is a live signal the true current scope may be larger.

cross_row_leads.facts: FERC issued a certificate authorizing Kinder Morgan/Tennessee Gas Pipeline's 'Mississippi Crossing' project (Docket CP25-514-000) on 2026-07-31: ~$1.7 billion, design capacity up to 2.1 Bcf/d, ~208 miles of 42-in and 36-in pipeline plus laterals and three new compressor stations, Greenville MS area toward Southeast markets -- matches this roster row's own numbers (Greenville->Alabama, 208 mi, 2100 MMcf/d) almost exactly. A FERC certificate is a strong status signal well past 'proposed' -- worth a status_review verdict toward construction/FID if not already reflected on P7802. Confirmed as a SEPARATE project/sponsor from P7833 (Energy Transfer/ETIH South Mississippi Project) despite the name overlap.

Same FERC certificate (Docket CP25-514-000, authorized 2026-07-31, ~$1.7B, up to 2.1 Bcf/d, ~208 mi of 42-in/36-in pipe + laterals, 3 new compressor stations) matches this row's recorded numbers (Greenville->Alabama, 208 mi, 2100 MMcf/d) as closely as it matches P7802's -- strong corroboration that P7802 and P7841 describe the SAME certificated Mississippi Crossing project (the orchestrator's suspected duplicate). Also note: FERC's companion project in the same docket family is 'South System Expansion 4' (Southern Natural Gas, Docket CP25-517-000, ~279 mi, also certificated by mid-2026) -- distinct from both P7802/P7841 and from P7833.
